tasks.title: First handler
tasks.statement:
Write a router with a single route: GET / responds with the text "hello". The main function (provided) sends two requests: to "/" and to a nonexistent path "/nope".

Expected output:
```
(200, "hello")
(404, "")
```
tasks.hint: Router::new().route("/", get(hello)); the handler is async fn hello() -> &'static str.

tasks.title: Path parameter
tasks.statement:
The route GET /rooms/{id} responds with "room N", where N is the number from the path (u32). For /rooms/abc axum returns a rejection by itself.

Expected output:
```
"room 7"
400
```
tasks.hint: Path(id): Path<u32>; for the format use format!.

tasks.title: Two path parameters
tasks.statement:
The route GET /rooms/{room}/msgs/{n} responds with «room=R n=N» (both u32). Use the tuple Path<(u32, u32)>.

Expected output:
room=3 n=15
404
tasks.hint: Path((room, n)): Path<(u32, u32)>.

tasks.title: Rest of the path
tasks.statement:
The route GET /files/{*rest} responds with "file: REST", where REST is the whole rest of the path (including slashes).

Expected output:
```
file: a.txt
file: docs/2026/report.pdf
```
tasks.hint: Write {*rest} in the path and Path<String> in the handler.

tasks.title: Query with default values
tasks.statement:
GET /msgs accepts a query string: limit (u32, default 10) and before (optional u64). The handler responds with «limit=L before=B», where a missing before is printed as «none».

Expected output:
limit=10 before=none
limit=5 before=none
limit=10 before=100
limit=3 before=7
tasks.hint: A struct with #[derive(Deserialize)], #[serde(default = "fn")], and Option<u64>; the extractor is Query<Page>.

tasks.title: Invalid query string
tasks.statement:
The route GET /page accepts ?n=number (u32, required) and responds with «n=N». Print the statuses for /page?n=5, /page?n=x, and /page (no parameter).

Expected output:
/page?n=5 -> 200 OK n=5
/page?n=x -> 400 Bad Request
/page -> 400 Bad Request
tasks.hint: Query<Params> with a field n: u32; an extractor rejection is 400.

tasks.title: Method not allowed
tasks.statement:
The route /rooms accepts only GET (response «list») and POST (response «created»). Print the statuses for GET, POST, PUT, and DELETE on /rooms and on /other.

Expected output:
GET /rooms -> 200 OK
POST /rooms -> 200 OK
PUT /rooms -> 405 Method Not Allowed
DELETE /rooms -> 405 Method Not Allowed
GET /other -> 404 Not Found
tasks.hint: get(list).post(create); a wrong method gives 405 by itself.

tasks.title: Custom 404 response
tasks.statement:
Add a fallback handler to the router: for any unknown path, status 404 and the body {"error":"not found"} (as a string). The route GET /health responds with «ok».

Expected output:
(200, "ok")
(404, "{\"error\":\"not found\"}")
tasks.hint: Router::fallback(handler); a tuple (StatusCode::NOT_FOUND, text).

tasks.title: 201 and the Location header
tasks.statement:
POST /rooms responds with status 201 and the header Location: /rooms/42, with the body "created". main prints the status, the Location header, and the body.

Expected output:
`201 Created Some("/rooms/42") created`
tasks.hint: The tuple (StatusCode::CREATED, [(header::LOCATION, "/rooms/42")], "created").

tasks.title: 204 with no body
tasks.statement:
DELETE /rooms/{id} responds with status 204 No Content and an empty body if id is a number; otherwise (for a non-numeric id) axum builds the response itself. Print the status and the body length.

Expected output:
```
/rooms/5 204 No Content body length 0
/rooms/x 400 Bad Request body length 40
```
tasks.hint: Return StatusCode::NO_CONTENT.

tasks.title: JSON response
tasks.hint: Json(Room { id, name }) with #[derive(Serialize)].

tasks.title: JSON request body
tasks.statement:
POST /echo accepts the JSON {"user":"name","text":"text"} (a Msg struct with Deserialize) and responds with "name: text (N chars)", where N is the number of characters (chars) in the text.

Expected output:
`anya: welcome (7 chars)`
tasks.hint: Json(m): Json<Msg>; the character count is m.text.chars().count().

tasks.title: JSON parse errors
tasks.statement:
POST /echo accepts the JSON {"n":number}. Print the statuses of axum's response to three bodies: a correct one, a syntactically invalid one (not JSON), and one with a wrong field type (n is a string).

Expected output:
200 OK
400 Bad Request
422 Unprocessable Entity
tasks.hint: Json<Num> with a field n: i64; rejections: bad syntax — 400, data doesn't fit — 422.

tasks.title: Custom response type
tasks.statement:
Implement IntoResponse for the enum Reply: Ok(String) → 200 and the text; Created(String) → 201 and the text; Gone → 410 with the body "deleted". The route GET /r/{kind} returns a Reply by kind: "ok", "created", or "gone" (anything else — 404).

Expected output:
```
ok: 200 OK good
created: 201 Created created
gone: 410 Gone deleted
zzz: 404 Not Found
```
tasks.hint: impl IntoResponse for Reply { fn into_response(self) -> Response { ... } }.

tasks.title: Result as a response
tasks.statement:
GET /rooms/{id}: rooms 1 and 2 exist (responses "room-1", "room-2"), all others get 404 with the text "no such room". The handler returns Result<String, (StatusCode, &'static str)>.

Expected output:
```
(200, "room-1")
(200, "room-2")
(404, "no such room")
```
tasks.hint: Err((StatusCode::NOT_FOUND, "no such room")) — a tuple can turn into a response.

tasks.title: Nested router
tasks.statement:
The function rooms() returns a Router with the routes GET / ("all rooms") and GET /{id} ("room ID"). Mount it under the prefix /api/rooms (nest). Print the bodies for /api/rooms and /api/rooms/9, and the status for /rooms.

Expected output:
```
all rooms
room 9
404 Not Found
```
tasks.hint: Router::new().nest("/api/rooms", rooms()).

tasks.title: Merging routers
tasks.statement:
There are two routers: users() with GET /users ("users") and rooms() with GET /rooms ("rooms"). Combine them in app() with the merge method, adding GET /health ("ok"). Print the bodies of the three paths.

Expected output:
```
/users: users
/rooms: rooms
/health: ok
```
tasks.hint: Router::new().merge(users()).merge(rooms()).route(...).

tasks.title: Fallback of a nested router
tasks.statement:
The API under /api answers unknown paths with its own 404 with the text "api: no"; the rest of the application outside /api answers with the text "app: no". The route GET /api/ping responds with "pong". Print the responses for /api/ping, /api/zzz, and /zzz.

Expected output:
```
/api/ping: (200, "pong")
/api/zzz: (404, "api: no")
/zzz: (404, "app: no")
```
tasks.hint: The nested router has its own .fallback(..), and the outer one has its own.

tasks.title: HEAD via GET
tasks.statement:
The route GET /info responds with "information". Print the status and body length for a GET request and for a HEAD request to /info (axum handles HEAD by itself).

Expected output:
```
GET: 200 OK, body present
HEAD: 200 OK, body empty
```
tasks.hint: You don't need to write a separate HEAD handler.

tasks.title: Custom response header
tasks.statement:
GET /ver responds with the body «v1» and the header X-Api-Version: 1. main reads the header from the response.

Expected output:
Some("1")
None
tasks.hint: The tuple ([("x-api-version", "1")], "v1").

tasks.title: Request header
tasks.statement:
GET /agent responds with "agent: ..." with the value of the User-Agent header, or "agent: unknown" if the header is absent. Use the HeaderMap extractor.

Expected output:
```
agent: curl/8
agent: unknown
```
tasks.hint: headers.get("user-agent").and_then(|v| v.to_str().ok()).

tasks.title: The whole request
tasks.statement:
The any-method handler for the path /whoami takes the entire Request<Body> and responds with «METHOD PATH», for example «POST /whoami?x=1». main sends GET and POST.

Expected output:
GET /whoami
POST /whoami?x=1
tasks.hint: axum::routing::any; req.method(), req.uri().

tasks.title: 409 on conflict
tasks.statement:
POST /rooms/{name}: the name "general" is already taken — respond with 409 and the text "busy"; any other name — 201 and the text "created". Check the general and an arbitrary case.

Expected output:
```
general: (409, "busy")
random: (201, "created")
```
tasks.hint: Return a tuple (StatusCode, &str) in both branches.

tasks.title: Handler with waiting
tasks.statement:
GET /slow/{ms} waits ms milliseconds (tokio::time::sleep) and responds with "waited ms ms". Three requests are sent concurrently (tokio::join!) with waits of 60, 20, and 40; main prints the responses in request order and "all within < 110 ms: true/false" (run in parallel, it should be faster than the 120 ms sum).

Expected output:
```
waited 60 ms
waited 20 ms
waited 40 ms
all within < 110 ms: true
```
tasks.hint: An async handler with sleep(Duration::from_millis(ms)).await.

tasks.title: Static path versus parameter
tasks.statement:
Routes: GET /rooms/new ("shape") and GET /rooms/{id} ("room ID"). The order of registration must not affect the result: the static path wins. Register the parameterized one first, then the static one, and print the responses for /rooms/new and /rooms/5.

Expected output:
```
shape
room 5
```
tasks.hint: matchit picks the most specific match regardless of order.

tasks.title: Redirect
tasks.statement:
GET /old responds with a redirect to /new (Redirect::to — status 303 and the Location header), GET /new — «new page». main prints the status and Location for /old.

Expected output:
(303, Some("/new"))
(200, None)
tasks.hint: axum::response::Redirect::to("/new").

tasks.title: All methods of a resource
tasks.statement:
The resource /rooms/{id} supports four methods: GET ("reading ID"), PUT ("changing ID"), PATCH ("editing ID"), DELETE ("deleting ID"). Use one .route call with the chain get().put().patch().delete(). Print the responses for all four methods on /rooms/8 and the status of POST.

Expected output:
```
GET: reading 8
PUT: changing 8
PATCH: editing 8
DELETE: deleting 8
POST: 405 Method Not Allowed
```
tasks.hint: get(h1).put(h2).patch(h3).delete(h4); handlers can be written as closures.

tasks.title: A real server on port 0
tasks.statement:
Start a server on 127.0.0.1:0 (TcpListener + axum::serve in a tokio task), find out the port, and send a plain HTTP/1.1 request "GET /hi" over a TcpStream with Connection: close. The handler responds with "hello from axum". Print the first line of the response (the status) and the last line of the body.

Expected output:
```
HTTP/1.1 200 OK
hello from axum
```
tasks.hint: tokio::spawn(async move { axum::serve(listener, app).await.unwrap() }); read the response with read_to_string.

tasks.title: Fix: body not last
tasks.statement:
The code doesn't compile: Json reads the body and must be the last handler argument. Fix the argument order so that POST /rooms/5/say with the body {"text":"hi"} responds with «5: hi».

Expected output:
5: hi
tasks.hint: Path first, Json last.

tasks.title: Fix: value not Send across await
tasks.statement:
The code doesn't compile: std::sync::MutexGuard is held across .await, and the handler's future must be Send. Fix it so the lock is released before the await (limit its scope with a block); the responses are "counter: 1", then "counter: 2".

Expected output:
```
counter: 1
counter: 2
```
tasks.hint: Take the value in a separate block { let mut g = ...; *g += 1; *g } before the sleep.
